title: p256-ecdlp: negation-quotient kangaroo with a charged instruction ledger

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), given only Q=[x]P on NIST P-256 with the SEC 2 Section 2.4.2 parameters (a=-3, r prime, cofactor 1), the two-animal kangaroo walk of proof.md on the quotient of the group by the negation map recovers x with probability at least 0.5. The walk keeps a canonical representative, so a class collision at scalar positions k1,k2 implies k1 = +-k2 (mod r); each collision yields exactly two candidates and both are verified by [x]P=Q. The tame trail stores T=2^128 canonical abscissas and the wild budget is 2*2^128 steps, charged in full whether or not it is used. All work is charged in AArch64 instruction equivalents divided by the fixed track constant C=1000, with P-256 field and point operations priced from their own instruction bounds rather than the borrowed secp256k1 addition price: total 3680494080616870420819859753982005332672512 instructions, so time_log2 = 131.435096, rounded upward at six decimals. Preprocessing is 1241350074527583514714390567911090787713024 instructions (preprocessing_log2 129.867106) and is included in the total with no amortisation. Peak memory is 2^134+2^20 bytes (memory_log2_bytes 134.000001); the stored trail is 2^133 bytes of nonuniform advice (133.000000) built by that charged preprocessing and included in peak storage. The single heuristic premise is the published expected-step bound E <= 2*sqrt(r/2) for a fully stored kangaroo trail, which Markov's inequality turns into the stated success probability. No quantum steps, uncharged oracles, external advice or amortisation over future targets are used.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustively check the quotient walk, the two-candidate collision resolution and the verification on the additive group Z_n for every scalar. This does not establish production curve behaviour, memory bounds, success probability or operation costs.
